segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Hello and welcome to Real Easy English, the podcast where we have real conversations in easy English to help you learn.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I'm Neil.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: And I'm Georgie. You can now watch this podcast and find a worksheet to help you learn on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: So, Georgie, how are you?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: I'm very tired actually. I've had a lot of social plans lately. How about you?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yeah, I'm fine. Social plans, that's interesting, because we're talking about friends today.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Yes, we're talking about socialising, which means spending time with people for fun. So,

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Neil, do you like spending time with friends?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yeah, I love spending time with my friends. If I don't see my friends very often, I feel

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: a bit sad and lonely so yeah i really like seeing my friends but i don't get to see them very often

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: because you know we're grown-ups and we have responsibilities

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: you have kids you have lots of

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: things going on i also like spending time with my friends i have lots of friends as i said i've had

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: a lot of social plans lately pretty much every day i been socializing

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: wow so you like socializing but do you like things like parties or do you prefer smaller social events

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: I do really like big parties because I like meeting new people

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: I like dancing as well.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: So at big parties, usually there's some music.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: But I do have a shy side of my personality.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: So usually a smaller event is better for me.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: so I can have kind of deeper conversations with fewer people.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: How about you?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yeah, I don't really like that situation

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: where you're at a party and don't know lots of people.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: So a small group of people that I mainly know

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: and there's one or two people who I don't know,

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: so, well, that's fine.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: But a bigger group with lots of people I don't know,

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I really don't like that.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: And why is that?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Is that because you don't like small talk?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yeah, I don't really like small talk.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: It feels a bit empty.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Small talk is conversations about things that aren't important,

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: like the weather, usually with people that you don't know very well.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yeah.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: And you don't like that.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: No, I find it awkward.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: So Georgie, you like meeting new people.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Do you feel embarrassed at all or are you completely fine with that

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: I think it depends I think if you find a topic quite quickly that you have in common that avoids embarrassment

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: But it's when you meet someone new, you don't know them very well, obviously, because they're

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: new, and you don't know what they like or don't like or what they think is rude or not

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: rude. But if you can figure that out quite quickly, it's usually okay. Do you usually

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: feel quite embarrassed then?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Sometimes. Like you said, it depends. If you find something

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: that you have in common, and you can talk about that, sometimes you don't find something

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: in common, and then it's really, I don't know, embarrassing, I suppose. Ooh, I feel strange

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: just thinking about it. You obviously, you like parties, you like socialising, but do you like

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: spending time alone?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: I get more energy from spending time alone and relaxing and not talking

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: to anyone. I often get what I call social burnout, which means you just get exhausted from spending

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: too much time with others. How about you?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Well, yeah, spending time alone is also important.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And I like to do that but not so much Not as much as maybe spending time with people because like I said before if I alone for too long

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I get a bit lonely and feel a bit, I don't know, just lacking energy.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Let's recap the vocabulary we heard in this podcast,

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: starting with socialise, which means to spend time with friends or other people to enjoy yourself.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: We heard small talk, which is conversation about things which aren't important,

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: such as the weather or the traffic. We use small talk a lot in the UK.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: We heard some adjectives to describe how you might feel about meeting new people.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: So we had embarrassed, which means feeling ashamed or shy.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And we also heard awkward, which means feeling uncomfortable when you're meeting new people.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: We also heard in common.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: So, if you have something in common with someone,

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: it means you share the same likes, dislikes or interests with someone.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: That's it for this episode of Real Easy English.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Test what you've learned by downloading the free worksheet on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Next time, we'll be talking about brothers and sisters.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: See you then.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Bye.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: you
